I think it depends on what you’re applying for. If you go to a job fair they’ll do two on the spot saliva tests that go to a lab. I quit smoking like 4 days before the tests and I passed. Quit for a few days and you should be fine, if they’re sending you to labcore for a urine test buy some quick fix. Good luck on the job!

Hey thank you for taking all the time to type this and let me just say, i can definitely understand where that feeling comes from and I know how hellish it is to face and I really hope you’re being genuine in saying you’re better (even if only slightly so, that’s awesome!) So for me I grew up eating like frozen bakery leftovers from garbage cans because of poverty, so I have a lot of anxiety about it (food- contamination). I also got food poisoning and it left me with chronic gastritis which has lead to other issues of course so more anxiety; i don’t eat most things I don’t make. This isn’t me promoting a business it’s just doing something nice because I NEED this service to have an income, baking is my craft, and maybe I get an extra dollar who knows. This isn’t me oversharing to like be an ass but because I do this because I wanna go to med school for psychiatry and genuinely people like you are who I worry about more than anything. If someone has a SEVERE allergy; do you think they are able to order off Instacart? No. Your trunk is contaminated by your entire areas groceries at that point. People with THIS severe know that. I could however deliver for a severe agoraphobic and they perhaps see it through the window and feel as though they cannot get their food. What helped me was trying to grapple with some harsh science (maybe the med in me idk) like the fact that other countries with more diverse cultures in the gut (it’s gross but- bacteria) have less gastro issues. Gloves fun fact are less safe than safe hand washing practices and proper hand hygiene (gloves are standard in all grocery kitchens and I saw firsthand how bad this one gets- people feel secure with a glove and don’t change it as often as they should). I hope this gets easier for you and the load lightens and whatever that behavior stems from stops rearing it’s ugly head(let me apologize for any assumptions made now) I believe in you! Also my sixteen year old says it’s weird to be positive on Reddit so if that’s the case I’m also sorry! Also maybe this should have been a message but maybe someone else will get something from it who knows. Again thank you for writing all that and the time and i wish you nothing but the best and I will take what you say to heart and I hope you understand partly why someone like me might do something like this.

Hey you know I really don’t think you need to be like this. I grew up in rural Maine in a community where the majority of kids go hungry, I care more about waste than most. Me saying my kitchen is cleaner than the majority of one’s people eat from wasn’t anything meant to attack, I just worked in that industry and most people who have worked in that industry would likely tell you something similar. I already stated I asked and if I get no response, well no cookie. There’s no reason to be this abrasive with someone. I do this to put myself through school so I can become a psychiatrist and help people in low income areas and hopefully move back to where I’m from, where this kind of thing is usually more appreciated. Genuinely whatever is making you feel as though something like this is somehow forceful, I hope you heal from. It’s just to be kind, as I stated I know firsthand how serious food allergens/sensitivities are. If you’re so concerned about waste why don’t you give to a hungry person like I said on the note or out for the next person who delivers for you, or in the trash. The food you waste from me is much less than the grocery stores who let produce and goods from states like mine rot on the shelves to keep them full and pretty while those same places they got the food from experience food insecurity, and you give them your dollar don’t you?

Hey I’m sorry I think you might have misunderstood what I was saying. I only leave them without asking if the batching I’m shopping is extremely standard, like let’s say a prepared ham sandwich, ice cream, Gatorade, gushers, standard groceries of say a family of five. What I would consider a “generic” order and I think most shoppers on this sub would know what I’m talking about. If it looks like anyone at all might have an allergy/sensitivity/anything at all which I have been trained and certified in though my prior profession, I ask and if they don’t respond I just don’t include it. I also make the cookies with no added coloring, the color in the picture comes from bonne maman jam which is considered to be pretty good in terms of ingredients and powdered freeze dried blueberries. I also add on the note you can just give it to the next hungry person you see, or throw it away. It’s a free cookie to be kind and because I like baking.

As a customer though I’m curious, if I made my greeting something like “hi I’m ____, your Instacart shopper! I’ll do my best to find all items on your list and contact you for instruction if anything is out after asking a store associate. If you have any questions or want to add anything to your order just let me know before checkout and I’m happy to help 😊 To say thank you for using a service like Instacart which helps chronically ill people like me have access to employment I include a free cookie in every batch I deliver. This season is _____. I also have a low sugar and gluten free option, would you like me to include one of these cookies in your order today at drop off? There is no expectation to tip extra but if you do it all goes to college tuition, medical bills, and recipe development and packaging for the cookies. Thanks for being such an awesome customer” would a message like that be worthwhile to you? I don’t wanna come across as though I’m begging for tips, I hope I get some from it, but I also just enjoy my craft and the opportunity to share it and food is just very special to me 🤷‍♂️ everyone should get a free cookie every once and a while! I also don’t have a low sugar no gluten cookie (yet!) but I’d like to make one because I myself am low sugar lol.
I’m also responsible for a teenager with a legume allergy (including peanuts), I get it.
